reader_task_results.authored_rationale: Hanriot247 places contested authority within military crisis; Maximum agitation250 supplies scarcity/price pressure and levy250 its popular demands and limits. Terror251/266 then gives the September response and contingent self-perpetuation. Carnot248 supplies practical capacity without making him sole cause.

Saint-Just252 distinguishes wartime revolutionary machinery,266 proposed and unimplemented redistribution,270 allegation-based Hébertist prosecution, and274 Dantonist indictment. Centralization263 supplies institutional context without projecting every measure onto one official.

Fouché259–260 and Chaumette261 retrieve local-to-Paris transmission, the calendar260 changed temporal setting, festivals261 coercive spread, and official opposition262–263 the freedom decree preceding Brie resistance and delayed compliance. The whole route preserves Grégoire, constitutional-clergy coercion and continuing closures.

Royal and Girondin252–253 trials and Tribunal270 demonstrate political management and prominent memory. Noyades257, suspect detention258 and Terror259 separately supply geographic concentration and differing approximate denominators, excluding Vendée war losses rather than adding them indiscriminately.

LawofSuspects251/258 supplies sweeping definitions, local knowledge and civisme. Its literal251→252 sentence supplies speech conformity; watchcommittees263 the reporting system. GeneralSecurity267 and useful268 release sentence continued269 establish independent Chabot imprisonment and Ronsin/Vincent release, not Robespierre’s automatic command.

Danton’s trial273–275 retrieves the corruption pretext, contested widening, vague charges and excluded defense, with explicit uncertainty about motives. RepublicofVirtue275 identifies potential-danger punishment and the harsher phase, not demonstrated guilt or consistent innocence.

Distinct city routes retrieve Marseilles commercial/sectional revolt, Lyons silk/provisioning crisis, Bordeaux republican hesitation, and Toulon dockyard grievances. Their248–255 trajectories contrast failed conciliation, mass reprisals, comparatively restrained commissions and later Bordeaux escalation. Bonaparte earlycareer206 explicitly supplies promotion after artillery success; Toulon255 supplies naval losses and strategic restraint. The named comparison supports these separate city routes without requiring a single general heading.

The crisis and programme routes explain contingent emergence; RevolutionaryGovernment263–264 gives central control and delayed enforcement; sansculotte decline271 and RepublicofVirtue275 explicitly establish that eliminating popular rivals did not end violence and could intensify it. Administrative design is not assumed to be instant effective control.

Hébert269–270 supplies single-section response and manufactured prosecution; decline270–271 supplies fatigue, achieved demands and paid service/state absorption. This answers failure of rescue independently of whether all earlier radical programmes are traced.

RepublicofVirtue272–273 gives law-bound direct action/delegation, public interest and equality as virtue. Danton274 and RepublicofVirtue275 connect moral suspicion to potential-danger punishment; Virtue276 supplies civic moral programme. This is continuation of coercion, not its replacement by rhetoric.

Chaumette’s direct named route traces subsistence leadership and religious initiative, then guarded reception of an isolated uprising, delayed congratulations and execution on presumed sympathy. Earlier radicalism does not prove organization of the March insurrection.

Hébert/Ronsin/Vincent and Billaud/Collot routes retrieve factional positions and changes; RobespierreIndulgents267–268 and Danton269 the broken moderation alliance. Fabre/Indies273 and trial274 distinguish proven fraud from politically widened allegations and poorly documented motives. Hébert249→250 newspaper clause is preserved as a source-binding referral, with actual useful249 and explicit250 access.
